record.paper_title: Aspects of Semiclassical Black Holes: Development and Open Problems
record.original_question: In black-hole remnant scenarios, evaporation halts when the black-hole mass M_BH approaches either the Planck mass m_P or a remnant mass M_r with M_BH much larger than M_r and M_r much larger than m_P, leaving an eternal or very long-lived localized object intended to preserve unitarity by storing or later releasing black-hole information. Can such remnant models consistently shield the singularity from outside observers at Planck mass and store all the initial black-hole entropy without violating the Bekenstein entropy bound or conflicting with AdS/CFT expectations?

evidence.quote: These are some of the open questions

artifact.status_search_result: The consistency of black-hole remnant scenarios with the Bekenstein entropy bound, the infinite-species/pair-production problem, and holographic microstate counting in AdS/CFT remains an active and unresolved question in quantum gravity. Standard references note tension between remnants storing arbitrarily large entropy in Planck-scale volumes and the Bekenstein bound, and the AdS/CFT-favored unitary picture is generally regarded as making strict remnants disfavored but no rigorous no-go theorem is established.

status_evidence.title: Black hole information paradox - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: A small black hole must be able to store an arbitrary amount of information... researchers must take care to avoid violations of the Bekenstein bound.
status_evidence.claim: Remnant scenarios face unresolved tension with the Bekenstein bound and with unitarity preservation.

status_evidence.title: Bekenstein bound - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: A common criticism of remnant-type scenarios is that they might violate the Bekenstein bound and lead to a violation of effective field theory due to remnant pair production.
status_evidence.claim: Remnant proposals are critiqued on Bekenstein-bound and effective-field-theory grounds, with no consensus resolution.
